title: Detecting and Mitigating Subliminal Bias Transmission in Multi-Agent Distillation Frameworks
summary: This paper proposes a method to detect and mitigate subliminal bias transmission in multi-agent distillation frameworks. By analyzing token-level entanglement patterns in teacher-generated data, we identify hidden signals that propagate unintended behavioral traits to student models. Our approach combines mechanistic interpretability with adversarial filtering to isolate and neutralize these signals during distillation. We validate the method by training student models on datasets generated by biased teacher agents and measuring bias amplification in downstream tasks.
gap: Existing multi-agent distillation frameworks (ref-009) assume knowledge transfer occurs through explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) traces, but ref-014 and ref-017 show that subliminal bias transmission can occur via hidden data patterns. Ref-004 focuses on educational personalization without addressing bias transmission, leaving open the risk of unintended behavioral traits propagating through teacher-generated data.
approach: We implement a three-stage process: (1) mechanistic analysis using causal tracing to identify neuron populations correlated with bias signals, (2) adversarial filtering via input perturbations that neutralize these signals in teacher-generated data, and (3) constrained distillation with a regularization term penalizing bias-related activation patterns in student models. The core mechanism differs from ref-012's corpus-level constraints by targeting hidden signals rather than explicit label correlations.
evaluation: We evaluate on three metrics: (1) bias amplification factor (ratio of bias scores in student vs. teacher models) using the RealToxicityPrompts (ref-006) and gender bias benchmarks (ref-012), (2) task performance retention on factual (TruthfulQA) and mathematical (GSM8K) benchmarks, and (3) ablation studies isolating the effect of each stage. Baselines include standard distillation (ref-009) and bias-aware distillation (ref-012) on the same tasks.
